title: Buffer allocation hypotheses: NA/EU/APAC Q3 experimental plan
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a short, fast-fail experiment plan for distributing buffer/warm-capacity across NA/EU/APAC in Q3 2026. Goal is to validate hypotheses about buffer sizing, lane isolation (staging vs warm vs on-demand), and cost/latency tradeoffs before locking into the wave-based provisioning schedule.

Context / why this is different:
- Existing capacity plans in the folder are schedule-heavy. This is intentionally hypothesis-driven: small, measurable experiments that we can run during the next 6–10 weeks and then adopt or discard.
- Focus is buffer allocation and the operational surface (how we use warm pools + short-lived on-demand vs long-reserved GPUs) rather than pure procurement cadence.

Key definitions used here:
- Reserved: long-term procured/reserved capacity (monthly/annual commits).
- Warm-pool: pre-warmed instances (kept available with minimal packing) that can take traffic within 2–5 minutes. Lower utilization target (20–50%).
- Staging-lane: dedicated smaller cohort used for experiments, can be preempted for reliability testing.
- On-demand burst: transient cloud on-demand instances to handle >95th percentile traffic spikes.
- Effective GPU: we count large instances (A100 80GB equiv) as 1.0; small quantized T4-like capacity as 0.15.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline demand forecast (conservative): 1.0M tokens/sec global sustained by July, with NA=50%, EU=30%, APAC=20% split.
- Avg tokens per second per effective GPU (sustained, production config): 3.5k toks/sec for medium-length chat workloads (median seq 256).
- Target steady-state utilization: 65% for reserved, 35% for warm-pool.
- Cost delta: warm-pool costs ~0.6x reserved (because smaller packing but idle hours), on-demand burst is ~1.8x reserved for short periods.

Primary hypotheses to test (fast-fail):
1) A 12% warm-pool of regional reserved capacity reduces P95 latency by >=12% during predictable traffic ramps vs no warm-pool.
2) Moving 8% of EU reserved into on-demand burst (keeping same total effective capacity) increases cost by <6% while reducing SLA miss count for EU by >30% during FRIDAY 16:00-18:00 surge windows.
3) Staging-lane isolation (1 GPU per 50 reserved GPUs) catches at least 60% of regression incidents before they hit production when used for canaries + fallback rehearsals.

Experiment matrix (week windows):
- Week 1–2: baseline telemetry collection (A/B control nodes active, no changes), capture P50/P95/P99 lat, cold-start failures, and token/sec per GPU.
- Week 3–4: NA: allocate warm-pool = 12% of reserved (move from reserved to warm-pool). EU/APAC unchanged. Measure latency delta and cost.
- Week 5: EU: convert 8% reserved -> on-demand policy for peak hours (set autoscaler policy). Run for Fridays only.
- Week 6: roll staging-lane across all regions (1:50 ratio) and run two canary flows: model rollout and kernel change.
- Week 7–8: analyze, revert, or scale; produce recommendation for wave provisioning.

Quick projection (experimental posture) — month-level snapshot (effective GPUs):
Month,NA_reserved,EU_reserved,APAC_reserved,NA_warm,EU_warm,APAC_warm,on_demand_pool,estimated_avg_util
2026-06,520,312,208,0,0,0,0,0.62
2026-07 (exp run 1),520,312,208,62,0,0,0,0.59
2026-08 (exp run 2),520,286,208,62,26,0,24,0.60
2026-09 (post-analysis),520,300,220,62,30,20,12,0.63

Notes on numbers above:
- Warm-pool columns show additional logical warm capacity (kept lightly packed) carved out from reserved budget for the experiment.
- on_demand_pool shows transient capacity initialized only during surge windows and autoscaled down outside.

Operational runbook (short):
- Preflight: create telemetry dashboards for per-region P50/P95, cold-starts, evictions from warm-pool, and per-model token throughput. Tag all test traffic with experiment_id=buffer-exp-2026q3.
- Deployment steps (per region):
  * Create warm-pool nodes via autoscaler pool config (label=warm-pool/experiment-buffer-exp).
  * Adjust routing weights: prefer warm-pool for requests where model pin matches and TTL in cache < 60s.
  * For on-demand experiments, configure scheduled autoscaler policy (Friday 15:30–18:30) with max surge nodes set to on_demand_pool.
  * Staging-lane: spin up 1 effective GPU per 50 reserved GPUs; wire canary flows (10% of new rollout traffic) through staging-lane first.
- Rollback criteria (any):
  * sustained P95 increase >10% for two consecutive hours vs baseline;
  * error rate spike >0.5% absolute;
  * cost burn for experiment >8% of projected monthly budget.

Metrics to collect (minimum):
- per-region: P50/P95/P99 latency (generation time), token/sec per GPU, per-request cost estimate, cache hit ratio (prefix+KV cache), node preemption rate, warm-pool idle percentage.
- business: SLA miss count, customer-facing error events, and cost delta vs baseline.

Success criteria (for adoption into wave plan):
- Hypothesis 1 confirmed: warm-pool reduces P95 by >=10% with <6% cost increase -> recommend 10–12% warm-pool target in wave provisioning for NA initially, then EU/APAC after verification.
- Hypothesis 2 confirmed: EU on-demand burst reduces SLA misses substantially at acceptable cost -> allow time-of-day autoscaler policies for EU peaks.
- Hypothesis 3 confirmed: staging-lane yields >50% early detection -> formalize 1:50 canary ratio.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Warm-pool rebalancing causes fragmentation and reduces sustained utilization. Mitigation: set minimum packing thresholds and run nightly consolidation jobs.
- Risk: On-demand surge costs spike unexpectedly. Mitigation: hard cost cap with immediate autoscaler drain at cap breach; alerting and runbook for Finance ops.
- Risk: Telemetry bias from test traffic. Mitigation: careful tagging, and mirrored production traffic for latency-only metrics.

Open questions (to resolve before week 3):
- Can we implement warm-pool eviction policy that prefers older KV caches vs newer ones? (Action: Ethan to prototype)
- What is the expected warm-up time for quantized T4-like nodes under current image build? (Action: Diego to measure cold boot + model load time)
- Who authorizes cost cap for Friday EU on-demand windows? (Action: Aisha -> finance on-call)

Checklist (TODOs):
- [ ] Create experiment telemetry dashboard (owner: Sana)
- [ ] Add experiment tags to routing layer (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Configure EU Friday autoscale policy (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Draft post-mortem template for each run (owner: Aisha)

Summary recommendation (if experiments succeed):
- Introduce regional warm-pool targets in wave provisioning (NA first at 10–12% reserved carve-out).
- Enable scheduled on-demand burst policies for region-specific peak windows (EU Fridays trial).
- Add staging-lane as standard canary surface at 1:50 ratio.

If experiments fail: revert warm-pool and on-demand changes and feed findings into next procurement sprint (notes to include detailed eviction/packing metrics).

Appendix: quick telemetry query sketches (pseudocode)
- P95 latency (region): SELECT percentile(latency_ms,95) FROM requests WHERE region="EU" AND experiment_id IS NULL OR experiment_id="buffer-exp-2026q3" GROUP BY 5m
- GPU token throughput: sum(tokens_generated)/(sum(active_gpu_seconds)/3600) -> tokens/sec per GPU.

END
